features.headline: Josh Allen leads Bills to win over tough Vikings defense
features.desc: The Vikings kept Allen in check for much of the game, but he helped the Bills earn a low-scoring victory.
body: MINNEAPOLIS — The NFL's stingiest defense made the NFL's highest-flying offense look pedestrian for four full quarters, but the Buffalo Bills somehow withstood the challenge and won the battle between two of the league's juggernauts.
Quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills outlasted the Minnesota Vikings for a 23-6 win on "Monday Night Football,"

retaining possession of the best record in the AFC at 7-1 despite a grind of a night when the Vikings held the Bills to a season low in points and 2 yards per play below their league-leading season average.
The Vikings (6-2) dropped their second straight in large part because of a listless offensive showing typified by quarterback Carson Wentz's 8.9 passer rating.

With the Vikings down three scores late in the fourth quarter, coach Kevin O'Connell benched Wentz for backup Max Brosmer, and the decision was met with near-universal approval from the restless home crowd.

The Bills entered Monday's action with the NFL's 30th-ranked passing defense but made a meal out of the overmatched Wentz, intercepting him twice, sacking him once and allowing him to complete fewer than one-third of his pass attempts.
Vikings fans booed Wentz after nearly every throw as the game went on, growing particularly restless in the fourth quarter as his accuracy further deteriorated.

As for the Bills' offense, coach Joe Brady built a game plan out of quick outlet throws and leaned heavily on running back James Cook III, who exceeded 30 carries for only the second time in his career with 31 rushes for 107 yards and a score.

features.headline: Cooper Flagg breaks down in-game peanut butter and jelly sandwich
features.desc: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg has recently started eating an in-game peanut butter and jelly sandwich.
body: With a comfortable lead against the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday, Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg headed to the bench for good early in the fourth quarter. He put on his warmups, sat next to teammate Daniel Gafford and watched the Mavericks close out a 130-93 victory.
Moments later, the Mavericks' TV broadcast caught Flagg with a small plastic bag in hand, taking out a peanut butter and jelly sandwich and having a bite.
"Boy, that looks good right now," former Mavericks guard Derek Harper said on the broadcast.
It marked the second consecutive game Flagg enjoyed a peanut butter and jelly sandwich during the action.

Last Friday, his in-game meal came during a 112-100 win over the Utah Jazz in which he racked up 21 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists and three steals. Cameras similarly spotted him taking a bite. Flagg followed that up with 25 points, a career-high 12 assists and five rebounds in Sunday's game.

Not surprisingly, reporters asked the second-year forward about his in-game snack. He first nodded to the Mavs' strength and medical staff before clarifying that he's trying to put on weight and gain muscle.

"So those requirements I got to meet. I'm just trying to stay ahead of it," Flagg said Sunday. "We got another game [Monday]. So just trying to get my calories and stay ahead of it and be ready for another one [Monday]."
Flagg said that he prefers smooth peanut butter and grape jelly. He added that he also enjoys sandwiches with peanut butter and banana, while sometimes adding honey.

features.headline: A 'confident' C.J. Stroud soaks in five-TD day against Chargers
features.desc: Stroud matched his career high with five TD passes and added 384 passing yards in the win.
body: HOUSTON — C.J. Stroud's five-touchdown performance against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday punctuated a hot start for the Houston Texans' quarterback.

Stroud & Co. were dominant in their 44-22 win, as he tied a career high in passing touchdowns to go with 384 yards passing, tied for his second most in a game. Stroud promised himself to "enjoy" his Week 9 performance rather than immediately moving on.

"I beat myself up a lot when I don't do great, so I'm going to enjoy this and celebrate with my friends, family and teammates because I know what it feels like to throw a couple interceptions," Stroud said.
"So, you need to be positive towards yourself.

Something that playing the quarterback position has taught me about life is that everyone could view you one way, but all that matters is how God views you and how you view yourself, so I'm grateful that God has allowed me to have some tough skin and be able to push through some tough times.
"Days like this come from being on the other side when you're not playing so great."
The Texans' 3-5 record isn't because of poor quarterback play. Through eight games, Stroud has had his strongest start to a season.

He has completed 64.2% of his throws for 2,251 yards, 16 touchdowns with only two interceptions, while posting a 104.8 passer rating, and he's on pace for career highs in passing yards and touchdowns.
Coach DeMeco Ryans said the fuel for Stroud's high-level performance is "confidence."
"You see the growth, you see the maturity in C.J.," Ryans said. "He's a top quarterback in this league because of that, because of his steadiness in the pocket, his resolve, his great energy all day.

features.headline: Who has won MLB Rookie of the Year? All-time winners list
features.desc: MLB's Rookie of the Year award is presented to the best rookies of the American and National League. Check out the full list of winners by year.
body: In 1947 and 1948, the Rookie of the Year was given to Major League Baseball's top rookie-eligible player. Since 1949, the award has been presented to a player in the American League and National League.
The Baseball Writers' Association of America votes on the award at the end of each season and before the start of the postseason.

Before 1957, voters used their own judgment to determine which players were considered rookies. After 1957, players were considered rookies if they had fewer than 75 at-bats or 45 innings pitched prior to the season.

This was later changed to 90 at-bats, 45 innings pitched or 45 days of MLB service time. In 1971, the mark was adjusted to 130 at-bats, 50 innings pitched or 45 days of non-September service time. That remains the standard today.
Jackie Robinson was MLB's first Rookie of the Year in 1947. Robinson hit.297 with 12 home runs, 31 doubles, five triples, 48 RBIs and 29 stolen bases for the Brooklyn Dodgers.
The award has been named the Jackie Robinson Award since 1987, the 40th anniversary of Robinson breaking the league's color barrier.

In 2026, Kevin McGonigle of the Detroit Tigers won the award for the American League, while Sal Stewart of the Cincinnati Reds won it for the National League. Here's a look at every rookie who has won the Jackie Robinson Award:
2023: Gunnar Henderson (AL), Corbin Carroll (NL)
2022: Julio Rodriguez (AL), Michael Harris II (NL)
2021: Randy Arozarena (AL), Jonathan India (NL)
2018: Shohei Ohtani (AL), Ronald Acuna Jr. (NL)

features.headline: Who will win MVP? Cy Young? Picks, analysis for 2026 MLB awards week
features.desc: Baseball's best players and managers of 2026 collect their hardware this week — starting Tuesday with the year's top rookies.
body: The baseball offseason has felt pretty normal so far, if you can put the overhanging labor negotiations out of your mind.
Some of that normalcy comes from the gradual easing into the initial phases of the hot stove season — contract options, roster maneuvering, free agency filing — that point toward next season.
That's administrative stuff, though, and not as fun as the parade in Milwaukee — or this week, when MLB hands out its major awards in what closes the books on the 2026 season.

This year's awards week adds a new honor being handed out by the Baseball Writers' Association of America: the Reliever of the Year Award, which recognizes the top bullpen maestro from each league. Here's how this week's schedule lays out:
Tuesday: Manager of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Wednesday: Cy Young and Reliever of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Thursday: MVP (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network)
MLB Network will also air the MLB awards given out during a live ceremony in Las Vegas at 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday.

Honors presented then include the Hank Aaron Award, Comeback Player of the Year, Mariano Rivera & Trevor Hoffman Relievers of the Year, Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter Award and selections for the All-MLB first and second teams.
Finalists for the major awards have already been announced. So let's see how things look before the hardware is handed out. Who might win? Who should win?

features.headline: NFL Week 9 arrivals: Justin Jefferson rocks black leather trench coat before 'MNF'
features.desc: NFL stars continue to turn gameday arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
body: November football doesn't come with one dress code.

The South could see two takes on fall fashion on Sunday. With sunshine and temperatures in the mid-60s in Charlotte, a varsity jacket or a knit polo would fit right in. In Miami Gardens, temperatures in the 80s leave room for breezy button-downs, relaxed trousers and shades.
Out West, sunshine in Southern California and the Bay Area sets the stage for short sleeves and lighter fabrics. Seattle could call for a different approach, with possible showers in the forecast.

The Northeast and Midwest offer more chances to break out fall staples. Temperatures in the 50s in Philadelphia and Foxborough are good territory for knitwear, and a cool Sunday night in Chicago gives players a reason to pull out a statement coat for the walk into Soldier Field.
Here are the NFL's most fashionable arrivals from Week 9.

Ahead of "Sunday Night Football," Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams wore a Supreme zip-up covered in varsity-style logo patches. Of course, Williams had an iced matcha in hand to complete his look plus a white cap.
On the other side, Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield rocked a plaid bomber jacket.
Campbell, who has been placed on injured reserve, said in a statement Wednesday that he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body.
